In 1929 Harry Hare, the first Belgrave President ever of the S.T.C.C.A., handed to his club mates the DEWAR Shield for winning the Championship (for the first time), and the six team winners medals to:- BILL MITCHELL (4), ARTHUR PENNY (7), ARTHUR ALLUM (12), BILL WEBB (16), PAUL KHLOPIN (23) and ALEC ROBERTSHAW (26).

Not so far away were BERT SHAW, ARTHUR ALLUM and JACK FLOWER; and we rejoiced that our nine men were all in front of Birchfield's sixth! On the last three mile lap many places were gained, the TAYLOR-SHIELDS-CARTER trio pegging back many positions.

Things were sorted out and the 80 year old turned out to be Cecil Mains (not to be confused with Dave) who was a cross-country man and my records show him as finishing 4th to Bert Footer, Arthur Penny and Arthur Allum in the 1933 10 miles Club Cross-Country Championship.

In the next three years Arthur Allum completed a hat-trick while Bert Footer took the record to 29.30 in 1935. The 'Belgravian' report that year captured the finish of the race in the style of prose of the day like this.
